cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, with a message for the Israelites. It's about one certain kind of sin, and what to do about it. Friend, I love a good system, and this is a WHOLE system.

cards.question: The LORD's message is about someone who sins against His commandments in what way?

cards.text: And first on the list? The anointed priest, and when HE sins, it brings guilt on the people. That's the smoke detector starting the kitchen fire, friend.

cards.question: For his sin offering, the anointed priest can bring any young bull, even one with a blemish.
The anointed priest brings his bull to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Before it's slaughtered, what does he put on the bull's head?

cards.text: Then the anointed priest takes some of the bull's blood and brings it into the Tent of Meeting. Not out front, friend, INSIDE.

cards.question: Inside the Tent, the priest dips his finger in the bull's blood and sprinkles some of it ___ times before the LORD, in front of the veil.

cards.text: Next, some blood goes on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense, right there in the Tent before the LORD. And there's still blood left over.

cards.question: Where does the anointed priest pour out the rest of the bull's blood?

answers.text: At the base of the altar of burnt offering
On the floor in front of the veil
On the ash heap outside the camp

cards.text: Then he removes all the fat, the same parts taken from the peace offering, and burns it on the altar of burnt offering. But that's not the whole bull.

cards.question: What happens to the rest of the anointed priest's bull, from the hide to the head to the legs?
The place outside the camp where the rest of the bull is burned is a ceremonially clean place.

cards.text: Now zoom out: what if the WHOLE congregation of Israel strays unintentionally, and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly? That's a group chat where EVERYBODY missed the same message.

cards.question: When does the whole assembly bring its sin offering?

answers.text: When they become aware of the sin
On the next day of rest
At the end of the year

cards.question: For the whole assembly, the sin offering is a young bull, the same animal the anointed priest brings.
One bull for the whole nation. The ___ of the congregation lay their hands on its head before the LORD.

cards.text: Then the anointed priest runs the same steps: blood into the Tent, seven sprinkles in front of the veil, blood on the horns, the rest at the base, fat on the altar. Same steps, and I respect it, because I've stamped the same cookie ten THOUSAND times and I still check the dough.

cards.question: For the whole assembly, the priest makes atonement on their behalf, and they will be ___.

cards.text: Then that bull goes outside the camp and gets burned, just like the first one. That's the sin offering for the assembly.
Next case: a leader sins unintentionally, and he incurs guilt too. Being in charge doesn't come with an undo button, friend.

cards.question: Once the leader becomes aware of his sin, what does he bring as his offering?
With the leader's goat, the priest carries the blood inside the Tent of Meeting, just like with the bull.
The priest burns all the goat's fat on the altar and makes atonement for the leader's sin. Then what happens for the leader?

answers.text: He must step down as leader
He waits seven days to be clean

cards.text: Now one of the common people sins unintentionally and incurs guilt. Regular folks, MY people, I came out of a bargain bin!

cards.question: When one of the common people becomes aware of his sin, he brings an unblemished ___ goat.

cards.text: Same steps as the leader: hand on its head, blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, all the fat burned as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. And he will be forgiven.

cards.question: If one of the common people brings a lamb instead of a goat, it has to be an unblemished male.

cards.text: Then the LORD gets specific: someone hears a public charge about something he witnessed, and he doesn't testify, so he bears the iniquity. That's the coworker who saw EXACTLY who took the parking spot and suddenly can't remember a thing.

cards.question: If someone touches something unclean, like the carcass of an unclean animal, without knowing it, he is still unclean and guilty.
In another case, a person's own words make him guilty. What does he do?

answers.text: Lies to a judge about a debt
Spreads a rumor about a friend

cards.question: If someone incurs guilt in one of these ways, he must ___ the sin he has committed.

cards.text: Then he brings a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering, and the priest makes atonement for him. But what if a lamb costs more than he's got?

cards.question: If a person can't afford a lamb for his sin offering, what may he bring instead?

answers.text: Two turtledoves or two young pigeons

cards.question: The person who can't afford a lamb brings two birds, and both are offered as sin offerings.

cards.text: The priest offers the first bird as the sin offering and prepares the second as a burnt offering, and the man will be forgiven. Same forgiveness, SMALLER wallet!

cards.question: And if a person can't even afford two birds, what may he bring as a sin offering?

answers.text: A tenth of an ephah of fine flour

cards.question: The flour for this sin offering gets no olive oil and no frankincense on it. Why not?

answers.text: Because it is a sin offering

cards.question: Even for the person who brings flour, the priest makes atonement and he will be forgiven.

cards.text: A handful of that flour goes up on the altar, and the rest belongs to the priest, like the grain offering. Stick around, friend, because this teaching on the offerings isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: "And first on the list?", "The anointed priest, and when HE sins, it brings guilt on the people." and "That's the smoke detector starting the kitchen fire, friend."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "On the ash heap outside the camp" tells the baker there is an ash heap outside the camp. That hints at the answer to card 11, where the rest of the bull is burned outside the camp, and at card 12, which asks about that place.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: No card tells or asks about Leviticus 4:24, 4:33-35 or 5:3. 4:24 covers the leader laying his hand on the goat and slaughtering it where the burnt offering is slaughtered. 4:33-35 covers the lamb's procedure, the atonement for it and the forgiveness. 5:3 is the case of touching human uncleanness. Because 4:24 is never told, card 7's "Same steps as the leader: hand on its head..." points back to steps the baker never heard.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This choice card comes right after the card about the male goat, and no story card says how the leader's goat is offered or where its blood goes. The baker has nothing to reason from when asked whether the blood goes inside the Tent, so the pick is luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: "I came out of a bargain bin!" is a callback to a backstory detail that was never set up in this lesson. Bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding, but they do not know about the bin. Tying "common people" to a bargain bin can also read as putting down regular folks.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The answers "female" and "male" are both the animal's sex, but "black" is a color. They are not the same kind of thing, and "black" is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says "Same steps as the leader" and lists the fat being burned "as a pleasing aroma to the LORD" as one of those steps. Leviticus 4:31 says "pleasing aroma" only for the common person's offering. The leader's offering in 4:26 doesn't say it, so the comparison claims more than the text does.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "hide" is not believable for something God's law requires, so it is silly and easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "repay" is close to the passage's own wording. Leviticus 5:7 calls the offering "restitution for his sin," so a baker could argue that he must repay the sin.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 19 already asks about Leviticus 5:13 and its forgiveness. Card 20 then steps back to tell 5:12, the handful of flour burned on the altar, and cites 5:12-13, which overlaps card 19. The story card goes backward instead of moving the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
